newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's China Airlines opens Beijing office.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's China Airlines opens Beijing office.

text.p: Taiwan's China Airlines has set up a representative office in Beijing to increase "business cooperation" with clients in China, local newspapers reported on Thursday.

China Airlines' Beijing office will handle customer service and sales for the airline in China, but it does not aim to promote direct links between the two sides, airline spokesman Yang Chen was quoted as saying by China Times.
The newspaper did not say when the office was established but added that several other Taiwan airlines, including EVA Airways, were also considering setting up offices in China.
Airline officials could not be reached for confirmation due to a national holiday in Taiwan on Thursday.

Taiwan has prohibited all direct links with China since a civil war separated the two sides in 1949 and turned them into political rivals. All flights must be routed through a third territory, usually Hong Kong, before arriving in China.
The head of China's state-owned flag carrier Air China in July toured Taiwan to explore cooperation with China Airlines and pave the way for direct air links.
China Airlines had said it hoped contacts with Air China would improve its prospects for pioneering direct flights to China.
Taiwan in June signed an air services accord with Hong Kong which some analysts said effectively ends Taiwan's ban on direct transport links with China.

Under the pact, the signing of which required Beijing's tacit approval, China Airlines and Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific will be able to continue flying lucrative Hong Kong-Taiwan routes after the British territory's return to Chinese rule in mid-1997.
The five-year deal also allows Hong Kong's Dragonair to fly to Taiwan.
